title: Ex Vivo Human Placental Explant Model for Controlled Exposure Studies
author: Ozarslan, Li, et al.
materials: 0.22 μm pore size vacuum filtration system

Timing: 1 h
1.Preparation of Cytowash and serum-free medium.a.Following the material tables, prepare 500 mL of Cytowash stock solution and 200 mL of serum-free medium stock solution.b.Filter each through separate 0.22 μm pore size vacuum filtration systems.c.Store the filtered Cytowash and serum-free medium stock solution at 4°C.2.Preparation of explant culture medium.a.Prepare explant culture medium (serum-free medium with 10% FBS) by adding 5 mL of FBS to 45 mL of serum-free medium.b.Mix thoroughly with a serological pipette.3.Preparation of exposure of interest solution.a.Prepare stock solution of exposure of interest such as drug, chemical, hormone, nutrient or pathogen, if applicable.
Optional: The exposure of interest will be customized for individual studies.

steps.title: Prepare Cytowash and serum‑free medium
steps.instruction: Prepare 500 mL Cytowash stock solution and 200 mL serum‑free medium stock solution as described in the material tables, filter each through a separate 0.22 µm vacuum filtration system, and store the filtered solutions at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 500 mL Cytowash stock solution.
Prepare 200 mL serum‑free medium stock solution.
Filter each solution through a 0.22 µm vacuum filtration system.
Store filtered Cytowash and serum‑free medium at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare explant culture medium
steps.instruction: Mix 45 mL serum‑free medium with 5 mL fetal bovine serum (final 10 % FBS) to obtain explant culture medium and mix thoroughly with a serological pipette.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL FBS to 45 mL serum‑free medium.
Mix thoroughly with a serological pipette.

steps.title: Prepare exposure stock solution (optional)
steps.instruction: Prepare a stock solution of the exposure of interest (drug, chemical, hormone, nutrient, or pathogen) according to the requirements of the individual study.

steps.title: Prewarm media and sterilize tools
steps.instruction: Prewarm the explant culture medium to 37 °C, sterilize fine scissors and forceps and keep them on ice, and set up the dissection microscope.

substeps.instruction: Prewarm explant culture medium at 37 °C.
Sterilize fine scissors and forceps; place them on ice.
Set up the dissection microscope.

steps.title: Set up 24‑well culture plates
steps.instruction: Determine the number and layout of wells needed in a 24‑well plate, add 500 µL prewarmed explant culture medium to each designated well (use separate plates for different time points if required).

substeps.instruction: Determine number and position of wells needed.
Plan the plate layout.
Add 500 µL prewarmed explant culture medium to each designated well.

steps.title: Transfer placental biopsy to ice‑cold Cytowash
steps.instruction: Remove the placental biopsy from the 50 mL conical tube, place it on a 100 mm petri dish on ice with cold Cytowash, and discard any basal plate if present.

substeps.instruction: Take the placental biopsy out of the 50 mL conical tube.
Place the biopsy on a 100 mm petri dish on ice with cold Cytowash.
Remove any basal plate if available.

steps.title: Dissect biopsy into 1 cm² pieces and wash
steps.instruction: Under the dissection microscope, identify stem villi, cut the tissue into ~1 cm² pieces, wash each piece 2–3 times with ice‑cold Cytowash to remove blood, and transfer the piece to a 35 mm petri dish containing ice‑cold Cytowash.

substeps.instruction: Identify stem villi under the microscope.
Obtain smaller ~1 cm² pieces.
Wash each piece 2–3 times with ice‑cold Cytowash.
Transfer the washed piece into a 35 mm petri dish with ice‑cold Cytowash.

steps.title: Isolate and spread chorionic villi
steps.instruction: Starting from the stem villi, carefully dissect the chorionic villi so they spread out, keeping them extremely fragile, avoiding excessive density, and trimming to ~10 mm × 10 mm if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Begin dissection at the stem villi and follow branching villi.
Dissect gently to keep villi intact and avoid excessive density.
Trim the villi to approximately 10 mm × 10 mm if needed.

steps.title: Place villi explants into culture wells
steps.instruction: Transfer each villus piece into a well of the prepared 24‑well plate containing 500 µL prewarmed explant culture medium and spread the villi evenly.

steps.title: Incubate explants before exposure
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates in a sterile CO₂ incubator set to 5 % CO₂ and 37 °C for 30 min prior to adding the exposure of interest.

description: The protocol below describes specific steps for isolating human placental explants from placental biopsies after delivery and setting up the explants for experimental exposures and conditions of interest. Safety data of multiple drugs and vaccines are limited in pregnancy as pregnant individuals are mostly excluded from randomized clinical trials. It is challenging to study the direct impact of drugs, chemicals, infectious agents, or other exposures on the human placenta, a unique maternal-fetal interface that is crucial for fetal development and healthy pregnancy. While no in vitro or ex vivo model can perfectly replicate the complex physiology of the maternal-fetal unit during pregnancy, the explant model maintains the physiological condition and structure of the placenta, serving as a useful method to investigate placental responses to experimental conditions. This protocol can be used to test the impact on placental tissue function of various factors under controlled conditions, including chemicals, hormones, drugs, nutrients, toxins, pathogens, and other conditions of interest. This part of the protocol describes the detailed dissection and culture of placental explants from the human placental biopsies. It is followed by the procedure for exposure of placental explants to the condition of interest. After treatment, the placental explants and culture supernatant can be collected for further downstream assessment.
